11.0.0.en: Moses stresses to the people that they must love God and keep His commandments, for this is the basis of their stability, their security and all the blessings they receive. This is the same as what Christ said: "If ye love me, keep my commandments" (Jn 14:15).

11.1.0.en: Moses declares to his hearers that he means those who were children under twenty years of age but were aware of the events in Egypt, that is, the ten plagues and the crossing of the Red Sea, and then all that happened in the wilderness of Sinai, and who did not die in Sinai with their fathers, who refused to enter the Promised Land and were those over twenty years of age. In these words he is not addressing those who were born in the wilderness of Sinai, nor those who were infants and small children not yet aware when they left Egypt, because he is speaking of events they saw that show the recompense of obedience or disobedience.

11.2.0.en: Moses addresses those who saw the ten plagues in Egypt, which proclaim that He is the only God who must be obeyed.

11.3.0.en: He made flow over: the waters of the sea rose and flowed over the army of the Egyptians.

11.3.1.en: He reminded them of His punishment of the Egyptians, who went out after God's people and were drowned in the Red Sea.

11.4.0.en: Moses also reminds them of God's works with them in the wilderness of Sinai, such as His punishment of Dathan and Abiram, of the tribe of Reuben, and those with them, who joined Korah in murmuring against Moses and Aaron because they alone held the priesthood (Num 16); the earth was cleft and swallowed them up, together with their families and their possessions. All these works of God they saw with their own eyes, and therefore they ought to obey His commandments and not disobey Him.

11.4.1.en: Remembering the punishment of the wicked and their end warns us to keep away from sin, which seems attractive but is very evil and destroys whoever practices it, and this makes us keep away from everything that leads to it.

11.5.s.en: (2) The good things of the Promised Land

11.5.0.en: The people were on the threshold of the Promised Land, so Moses draws their attention to the importance of obeying the word of God, so that they may possess the new land and settle in it for many years and enjoy its good things, symbolized by milk and honey.

11.6.0.en: Wateredst it with thy foot: he moves the mud aside with his foot and opens the irrigation channels inside the field, and after these basins are watered he closes the channels with his foot with an amount of mud, so that the water is diverted to the next basins to water them. Plains: the valleys.

11.6.1.en: God declares to them that the way of watering the land in Egypt depends on the waters of the Nile, which water it easily like fields planted with vegetables. But in the land of Canaan most agriculture depends on the rain water that God gives in its season, which makes people depend on God who gives it. So when they obey Him, His blessings pour down on them from heaven throughout the year, and the land is filled with crops and good things.

11.6.2.en: One of the loveliest phrases of this book is the phrase "The eyes of the LORD thy God are always upon it, from the beginning of the year even unto the end of the year." How much the Lord cares for us and provides for our needs, not only at certain moments but throughout all the days of our life on this earth; He knows all our material needs and supplies them to us at the right time. May we in our prayers seek first the Kingdom of God, confident of God's care for us, for He gives us more than we ask or think.

11.7.0.en: The first rain: at the beginning of the winter planting season, that is, in the month of October, so that the seed may grow.

11.7.1.en: The latter rain: before the harvest, that is, in the month of March, to complete the growth of the plants.

11.7.2.en: Grass: fodder plants such as clover.

11.7.3.en: If you obey God's commandments, He gives you the rains in their due time needed for the growth of the plants, and you will obtain abundant crops of wheat, grapes and olives. The fodder plants needed to feed the animals also grow, so that they become big and fat, which provides all the food needed by God's people.

11.8.0.en: Be deceived: be tricked and lust.

11.8.1.en: He warns them against the worship of idols, lest they think that they are the cause of the good things of the land of Canaan, as the pagan peoples living around them say; for then God withholds the rain, and the land dries up and does not yield its crops, and man hungers and perishes.

11.9.0.en: Here he repeats what he mentioned in (ch. 6:6-9), which is the importance of remembering God's word and repeating it all day long.

11.10.0.en: As the days of heaven upon the earth: that is, forever; what is meant is a long life.

11.10.1.en: God gives him the good news that if he obeys the commandment which he repeats all day long, He will grant him a long life in the Promised Land and afterward life in the new land, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

11.11.0.en: God promises them that if they love Him, obey His commandments and walk by them, He will drive out the pagan peoples, the inhabitants of the land of Canaan, from before them and will give them possession of their land, even though these are strong and great peoples.

11.12.0.en: Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: a figure for their not being forced to withdraw from any lands they take possession of.

11.12.1.en: The uttermost sea: the Mediterranean Sea.

11.12.2.en: An incentive and encouragement from the Lord to them to advance forward without fear of retreat or defeat before the enemies. What they take possession of in lands they will not lose, but they will continually advance forward from victory to victory.

11.12.3.en: And the Lord defines for them the boundaries of the land promised to them as follows:

11.12.4.en: On the south, the wilderness, that is, the wilderness of Sinai.

11.12.5.en: On the north, the mountains of Lebanon.

11.12.6.en: On the east, the river Euphrates.

11.12.7.en: On the west, the Mediterranean Sea.

11.12.8.en: (Note: Israel did not reach this extent except in the reign of Solomon (1 Kgs 4) (map 17).

11.13.0.en: No military commander who fights you will be able to hinder your advance. And the news of your swift, decisive victories in the battles you wage will be spread, which makes the peoples in the region fear you and tremble at meeting you.

11.13.1.en: Obeying God's commandments gives you awe in the eyes of those around you, so that they fear to wrong you and respect your word, and you have an opportunity to teach them God's word through your conduct and your ordinary words.

11.14.0.en: The Lord places Israel at a crossroads to choose between two ways that cannot be combined: a way that leads to enjoying the divine blessings, and a way that brings the curse.

11.15.0.en: The first way is the way of obedience to the commandments that Moses conveyed to them from the Lord, which he always reminds them of and repeats to them again today.

11.16.0.en: The second way, in which many curses befall them, is their neglect of God's commandments and their abandoning the worship of Him for the worship of strange gods, that is, idols.

11.17.0.en: Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal: two mountains south and north of Nablus (Shechem), separated by a narrow valley.

11.17.1.en: After you enter and possess the land which the Lord leads you to take, stand between Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. From these two places, which lie in the middle of the Promised Land, the blessing and the curse are proclaimed, as though the two mountains stood as silent witnesses to the renewal of the covenant.

11.17.2.en: The blessings and the curses are mentioned in detail in (ch. 27:11-26).

11.18.0.en: Beyond Jordan: the western side of the Jordan.

11.18.1.en: A detailed description of the location of the two mountains, Gerizim and Ebal: they are on the western side of the Jordan River, while Moses and the people were standing on its eastern side. From the place where Moses and the people stood, they could see the sun as it sets and disappears behind the two mountains.

11.18.2.en: Behind the way where the sun goeth down: that is, toward the west.

11.18.3.en: In the land of the Canaanites, which dwell in the champaign: the Arabah is the low valley on the two banks of the Jordan River north of the Dead Sea (map 18). Over against Gilgal: the land of Gilgal is about 13 km north of Bethel. What is meant here is the other region.

11.18.4.en: The plains of Moreh: the site of the great oak tree where Abraham pitched his tent when he entered Canaan (Gen 12:6), near Shechem.

11.19.0.en: For you are about to cross the Jordan to take possession of the land which God has given you. Your permanent settlement in this land depends on your care to complete the statutes which I commanded you and to apply the judgments which I have set for you.

11.19.1.en: With the end of the eleventh chapter, the second sermon of Moses the prophet ends, which began at the end of the fourth chapter from (v. 44). This sermon spoke as a whole about keeping the commandments and keeping away from what hinders them.

11.19.2.en: God wants to bless your life if you walk with Him and keep His commandments, so do not reject Him for the evils of the world or its passing delights, and do not persist in sin in contempt, exposing yourself to His divine punishment; for despite His constant mercy, He is also perfect in His justice.

11.19.3.en: The offerings in the house of the Lord

12.0.s.en: (1) Removing the idols and worshiping God

12.0.0.en: From this chapter on, various laws are mentioned, and in this chapter he concentrates on the worship of God and the offerings presented to Him. From here begins the third sermon of Moses the prophet, which extends to (ch. 27:10) and speaks about the laws and ordinances that must be applied when they enter the land of Canaan, and this sermon is considered the core of the book.

12.1.0.en: God commands His people to remove every trace of the worship of idols, whether on the mountains, the hills or under the trees.

12.2.0.en: Pillars: stone columns set up for idols.

12.2.1.en: Groves: wooden columns set up for idols.

12.2.2.en: The Book of Deuteronomy. God continues His discourse about removing the worship of idols, and commands that the pagan altars, images and pillars be destroyed and the groves burned. Removing the idols is necessary to purify the people's thought so that they may worship God, the only God.

12.3.0.en: To put his name: to declare Himself.

12.3.1.en: His habitation: in it the divine presence and holiness.

12.3.2.en: He commands them, in their worship of God, not to set up images for Him as the worship of idols is done everywhere, but in the place that God appoints they are to offer communal worship, and not in any other place. What is meant by this is:

12.3.3.en: 1- Affirming the oneness of God and rejecting the idea of a multiplicity of gods, such as a Baal for every pagan city.

12.3.4.en: 2- The unity of the people in their worship of God.

12.3.5.en: 3- Keeping them away from the worship of idols that is widespread around them among the pagan peoples.

12.4.0.en: Burnt offerings: sacrifices that are burned entirely.

12.4.1.en: Sacrifices: what is slaughtered of the animals of the offerings.

12.4.2.en: Tithes: a proportion of one to ten of income, which was required to be offered to the Lord and given to the priests and the Levites.

12.4.3.en: Heave offerings of your hand: the offerings and oblations that are lifted up to the Lord.

12.4.4.en: Vows: what a person pledges between himself and himself to offer to God if his request is fulfilled.

12.4.5.en: Freewill offerings: voluntary offerings (more than the Law requires) that a person offers out of love for God. Firstlings of your herds and of your flocks: the first-born of the animals that are offered to God.

12.4.6.en: Ye and your households: your wives, your sons and your servants.

12.4.7.en: The people must offer their various offerings in the place that the Lord appoints, and what was eaten of them was eaten before the Lord, that is, in His presence. This was an occasion for joy and gladness and for giving thanks to the Lord for all His gifts, blessings and graces which He pours out upon His people.

12.4.8.en: God's love and humility shine forth in His being present in His Church, waiting for His people to come to Him. So hasten to the bosom of the Church to enjoy the presence of God and to pour out your love and all your needs before Him, and you will receive an inexpressible blessing.

12.5.s.en: (2) Offerings to God and eating meat

12.5.0.en: Here this day: that is, in the wilderness of Sinai.

12.5.1.en: The rest and the inheritance: that is, the land of Canaan.

12.5.2.en: The application of the Law in the wilderness of Sinai differed from its application in the land of Canaan, where all the feasts are held and the people are not bound to sprinkle the blood of any sacrifice they slaughter for eating on God's altar, as used to happen in Sinai because of the distance between their dwellings and God's altar.

12.6.0.en: He stresses to them that after they enter the land of Canaan, finish their wars, take possession of the land and settle in it, they must be committed to offering all their offerings to the Lord in the place that God appoints for His house, that is, the tabernacle of meeting, so that they and their families may rejoice in the worship of God and eat of the sacrifices, they and the Levites who take their share of these sacrifices and offerings.

12.7.0.en: He repeats a second time that the offering of sacrifices and offerings must be in the house of the Lord, whose place God appoints in one of the tribes of the children of Israel, that is, in the land they will possess, and no sacrifices are to be offered in any other place. He stresses this matter many times because, sadly, after they entered and took possession, and after the death of Joshua, the Book of Judges tells us that they were not committed to this, but each one did what he saw fit (Judg 17:6, 21:5).

12.8.0.en: Within any of thy gates: all your houses.

12.8.2.en: The hart: the mountain buck, a kind of mountain goat resembling gazelles, which runs swiftly and has great need of drink and food or else its body grows faint.

12.8.3.en: The unclean: animals that are clean but are not permitted to be offered as sacrifices to God, since God specified what is offered to Him, such as the bull, the sheep and the goat. It can also mean a person who has been made unclean by any cause, such as an issue of blood or the like.

12.8.4.en: When they slaughtered any animal to eat in the wilderness of Sinai, they sprinkled its blood on the altar because of the nearness between the tents and the altar, but after they took possession of the land of Canaan, some of the tribes dwelt far from the altar, so God permitted them to slaughter animals for eating from among the clean animals, whether those permitted to be offered to God or not, and to pour out their blood on the ground and cover it with dust, as mentioned in (Lev 17:13). He also permits the eating of this meat to the clean person or to one who has been made unclean by any cause, because it is merely food and not a sacrifice offered to God.

12.9.0.en: He repeats a third time that the offering of tithes, firstfruits, vows, freewill offerings and heave offerings must be in the house of the Lord only, and the one who offers it eats of what the Law permits him, he and his family, his servants and the Levites, before the house of the Lord in the holy place and not in his own house.

12.10.0.en: The Lord warns not to neglect the Levite's share of the offerings and tithes, for since he was not given a portion of the land like the rest of the tribes, he has a right to the good things of the land like the rest of his brethren of the other tribes, in that he eats his share of the offerings and sacrifices offered to God.

12.11.0.en: The LORD thy God shall enlarge thy border: you took possession of the land of Canaan with its wide boundaries.

12.11.1.en: Here he confirms what he mentioned in (v. 15), that after they possess the land of Canaan and dwell in places far from the house of the Lord, they may slaughter clean animals in their homes to eat of them, whether those permitted to be offered to the Lord or those not permitted, and the clean person or the unclean may eat of them.

12.12.0.en: He stresses again that the blood is not to be drunk when animals are slaughtered to be eaten as ordinary food in their homes; they are to pour out their blood on the ground and cover it with dust and not drink of it, for the following reasons:

12.12.1.en: 1- Blood represents the life of the animal, which God created, so out of respect for this life granted by God, they do not drink it.

12.12.3.en: 2- It is a type of the blood of Christ, so they do not drink it, in sanctification of it; and in the New Testament the blood of Christ is given to the believers as life for them through the sacrament of Holy Communion.

12.12.4.en: 3- Drinking blood stirs up a person's lusts and instincts.

12.12.5.en: 4- Blood transmits some diseases, so not drinking it protects against them.

12.12.6.en: 5- So that they may not share with the pagans who drink blood in some of their worship.

12.12.7.en: And when they obey this commandment, they receive many blessings and good things.

12.13.0.en: Thy holy things: the sacrifices offered and set apart for God.

12.13.1.en: Here too he confirms that the offering of sacrifices to God is to be in His house, in the place that He appoints in the land of Canaan. The blood of the animals is poured out on the altar, and those who offer the sacrifices eat of them in the holy place in the house of the Lord.

12.14.0.en: God confirms His promises of blessings to His people if they obey these commandments.

12.14.1.en: God cares for the food of His children and not only for their worship. So abide in your relationship with God, confident of His providence and care for all your affairs, and keep His commandments with precision, and you will receive countless blessings.

12.15.s.en: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

12.15.0.en: After God destroys the pagan inhabitants of the land from before His people and they possess their land, He warns them against taking part in the worship of their idols and inquiring about its details in order to imitate them.

12.16.0.en: He forbids them to imitate the methods of pagan worship, for they are defiled methods which the Lord abhors, among them offering human sacrifices of their sons and daughters as offerings to the pagan gods.

12.17.0.en: God warns them to carry out His commandments with all exactness, neither adding to them nor taking from them for any personal purpose.

12.17.1.en: Do not imitate the people of the world in their evil words and their wrong methods, but keep yourself pure in thought, word and deed, because you are the light of the world and the salt of the earth.

12.17.2.en: Putting to death whoever turns the people away from the worship of God (1) The false prophet (vv. 1-5:) 1 "If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder, 2 And the sign or the wonder come to pass, whereof he spake unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods, which thou hast not known, and let us serve them; 3 Thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams: for the LORD your God proveth you, to know whether ye love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul. 4 Ye shall walk after the LORD your God, and fear him, and keep his commandments, and obey his voice, and ye shall serve him, and cleave unto him. 5 And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from the LORD your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the LORD thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee."
